title: Title: 2 months of solo dev on my multiplayer bending game (July greybox → now)
author: Odd-Childhood1824

replies.author: Odd-Childhood1824
replies.body: Oh nice, I had to look that one up! 😂

comments.author: Significant_Tell407
comments.body: This isnt bending imo. I feel like alot of players try to emulate what being is simply by having a character throw elemental projectiles after a martial arts ability. But this just isnt the high people are standing for. What happens if there is a fight in a burning village? Can the fire bender control that fire? What is a water bender is near a lake? Can they manipulate the water to create more profound attacks and defenses? Idk to me bending is about control and manipulation not just throwing blobs of elements.  Your elements need alot more polish. They dont move or behave like the corresponding elements you create. You need also a better control mechanism other than mashing b to attack

replies.author: drallcom3
replies.body:
> This isnt bending imo.

Looks like a shooter blueprint with fireballs added in. I was expecting combos or literal bending. This here is someone using UE for the first time. Good for them, but won't earn you applause.

replies.author: Odd-Childhood1824
replies.body:
Fair enough, I can see why it comes across that way at this stage. I'm two months into development, learning UE from scratch, and this is very much an early prototype rather than a representation of where I want the game to end up.

I'm not looking for applause for what it is right now. I'm sharing the progress to get feedback, learn from it, and hopefully build something that actually delivers on the fantasy. There's a long way to go, but that's the point of sharing the development this early!

replies.author: i_rate_slop
replies.body: Hmm… 🤔

replies.author: Odd-Childhood1824
replies.body: Haha, fair reaction 😂 Still very much a work in progress!

replies.author: i_rate_slop
replies.body: Oh no I liked yours, but this persons comment made me start wondering how one would actually make something like they described.

replies.author: Odd-Childhood1824
replies.body:
Hahaha well yeah, that's exactly the kind of rabbit hole I've been going down 😂 I'm a huge fan of the Avatar universe and the whole idea of bending, so the original fantasy was literally just being able to throw a fireball and control it a bit. When I finally got that working, I started thinking… okay, but how do I turn this into a whole fighting game? ... 😂

And that's where the real challenge begins! There are so many crazy possibilities with elemental manipulation, interactions, combos, movement, counters, etc. It's a lot to figure out, especially as a solo dev learning Unreal Engine along the way.

I guess the only way is step by step, testing ideas, sharing the progress, and hopefully building a community of people who are excited about the vision and can help shape it. There's a long way to go, but that's part of the fun!

replies.author: Significant_Tell407
replies.body: I have already done it but dropped the project to work on another idea. Instead of trying to rely on martial arts you need a refined control scheme and then the martial arts becomes secondary. By this i mean I create a "painting" tool that allows you to pull and manipulating the element you are controlling. Imagine a WoW aoe circle but upon pressing allows you to control the element in that area. Much more effective and actually feels like you are bending. Then when you release the martial arts plays but its not really an old school button mashing fighting because thats not the focus in a projectile bending game

replies.author: Odd-Childhood1824
replies.body:
I actually agree with you, and this is pretty much the direction I want to take it. For me, bending is about manipulating and controlling the elements, not just throwing projectiles, and I definitely want environmental interactions and more freedom in how you use each element.

I'm still very far from that vision, though. This is the result of my first two months of development, and I'm learning Unreal Engine along the way, so even getting the basics working is a challenge right now 😅

The goal is to make that bending fantasy feel real while keeping the game easy to pick up but hard to master, especially in a competitive arena mode. I know there's a lot to improve, and feedback like this helps me figure out what matters most. Appreciate the input!

replies.author: PieMastaSam
replies.body: This is some god tier feedback to get from someone early imo.

comments.author: twendah
comments.body: How you solve the serverside checking on all these events to keep the gameplay fluent?

replies.author: Odd-Childhood1824
replies.body:
Honestly, I'm not that far into the networking side yet, so I don't have a definitive solution for it at this stage.

I've done some testing with friends, and the basic projectile gameplay feels pretty decent so far. The current bending mechanic also lets you influence the projectile's path with mouse movement, so there's more going on than just firing in a straight line.

But I know making that feel responsive while keeping everything server-authoritative and fair in competitive play is a whole different challenge. That's something I'll need to properly tackle as the mechanics evolve. Definitely one of the big things I'm keeping in mind!

comments.body: Great work so far, I’d love to see some more in depth bending, similar to what other comments said. I know you’re still early so it’s hard to judge it at this point. replies.author: Odd-Childhood1824

The mentality you are describing is exactly how I want the game to be. When I will finally avec an MVP ready for all elements I think it will become clear what we can expect from the game. comments.author: Inevitable_Ranger745
comments.body: Looks like you’re cookin!, mind if I ask what your animation workflow looks like?

replies.author: Odd-Childhood1824
replies.body:
haha thanks! Still trying to figure that out myself... I'm using a Martial Arts animation pack as a base and currently trying different workflows: Mocap & Keyframing but my results are still mediocre for both.

Later in the project when the MVP is available as a demo and the game is proven to be "fun and competitive" I can look at ways to Polish everything, currently just trying to find animations that are close enough to the feeling of being a pro bender! :)

replies.author: Odd-Childhood1824
replies.body: It's definitly a challenge because Avatar is based on 4 different martial arts, depending on the element. And my basic Martial Arts pack covers the fire bender moves the most. Waterbending is Tai Chi and I didn't find any cheap or free resources for that currently. For waterbending I'm currently experimenting with sword animations that I found for free, close enough for now! haha
